questions.stem: The Union Cabinet's clearance for sale of a majority stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings has been described as the biggest privatization since Air India. In this context, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM), under the Ministry of Finance, oversees the Central Government's disinvestment process.
IDBI Bank was reclassified by the RBI as a private sector bank after the Life Insurance Corporation of India acquired majority ownership in it.
The Tata Group's acquisition of Air India, completed in 2022, was India's first strategic disinvestment of a public sector bank.
Strategic disinvestment involves the government selling a stake along with transfer of management control to a private buyer.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: DIPAM handles disinvestment, IDBI Bank was reclassified as private after LIC's 2019 majority stake acquisition, and strategic disinvestment by definition includes transfer of management control. Statement 3 is wrong because Air India is an airline, not a bank, so the claim misdescribes the category of asset.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: The week in charts: Jio's mega debut, deferred UPI charges, IDBI bank stake sale
questions.pyqLink: Tests strategic disinvestment policy and DIPAM's role, similar to UPSC 2020 prelims question on disinvestment and strategic sale.

questions.stem: Following the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site and the MHA's directions to States on preventing mobilisation of protesters, consider the following statements regarding the right to peaceful assembly in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution guarantees citizens the right to assemble peaceably and without arms.
This right can be exercised with arms if prior police permission has been obtained.
Reasonable restrictions on this right can be imposed only through a constitutional amendment, not by ordinary legislation.
Public order, and the sovereignty and integrity of India, are grounds on which the right to assembly may be reasonably restricted.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: Article 19(1)(b) guarantees peaceable, unarmed assembly, and Article 19(3) permits reasonable restrictions on grounds including public order and sovereignty/integrity of India. Statement 2 is false since the right explicitly excludes assembly with arms, and statement 3 is false because restrictions are imposed through ordinary law (e.g., Section 163 BNSS), not constitutional amendment.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Ministry of Home Affairs directs States to prevent CJP supporters from mobilising towards Delhi
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 19(1)(b) and 19(3) reasonable restrictions, akin to UPSC questions on fundamental rights and their limitations.

questions.stem: World Bank President Ajay Banga addressed the institution's 2026 Annual Meeting in Bangkok. With reference to the World Bank Group, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The World Bank Group consists of five constituent institutions, including the International Development Association (IDA), which provides interest-free loans and grants to the world's poorest countries.
The President of the World Bank Group is elected by a majority vote of the United Nations General Assembly.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the World Bank Group comprises IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID, with IDA serving the poorest countries. Statement 2 is incorrect because the President is selected by the Bank's Board of Executive Directors, not the UN General Assembly, and by convention has been a US nominee since the US is the largest shareholder.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: 800 million jobs at risk over 15 years? World Bank's Ajay Banga calls for global financing overhaul
questions.pyqLink: Tests structure of Bretton Woods institutions, similar to UPSC questions distinguishing IMF, World Bank, IBRD and IDA.

questions.stem: NPCI's deferment of charges on select UPI person-to-merchant transactions has drawn attention to India's digital payments architecture. Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) was set up as the umbrella organisation for operating retail payment systems in India under the guidance of the RBI.
NPCI is registered as a not-for-profit company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.
As per extant government policy, Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) is currently applicable on all UPI person-to-merchant transactions, regardless of transaction value.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NPCI is the RBI/IBA-promoted umbrella body for retail payments, incorporated as a Section 8 not-for-profit company. Statement 3 is incorrect because the government's zero-MDR policy has applied to UPI transactions since January 2020, and the recently deferred proposal concerned only select high-value P2M transactions, not all transactions.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: The week in charts: Jio's mega debut, deferred UPI charges, IDBI bank stake sale
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional architecture of digital payments regulation, akin to UPSC questions on RBI, NPCI and UPI.

questions.stem: The World Bank has announced plans to quintuple its critical minerals financing, echoing India's own push under the National Critical Mineral Mission. Consider the following pairs of critical minerals and their primary industrial use:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Primary raw material in solar photovoltaic panel glass
Manufacture of permanent magnets for wind turbines and EV motors
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correctly matched: lithium is central to EV batteries, graphite serves as the standard anode material, and rare earths like neodymium are used in permanent magnets. Pair 2 is incorrect because cobalt is primarily used in battery cathodes, not solar panel glass, which is made of low-iron glass.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: 800 million jobs at risk over 15 years? World Bank's Ajay Banga calls for global financing overhaul

questions.stem: Kevin Warsh's remarks on AI reshaping the global economy draw attention to how governments are institutionalising AI policy. With reference to India's policy response, which one of the following best describes the IndiaAI Mission?
options: It is a legally binding international treaty signed by India to regulate cross-border data flows used in AI training.
It is a Central Sector Scheme approved by the Union Cabinet, under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, to build a national AI compute and innovation ecosystem.
It is a regulatory authority set up under the Information Technology Act, 2000 to license commercial AI models before their release.
It is a NITI Aayog-administered venture capital fund that directly takes equity stakes in private AI startups.
questions.explanation: The IndiaAI Mission is a Central Sector Scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in 2024, implemented by MeitY, aimed at building AI compute infrastructure, datasets platforms and innovation support. It is neither a treaty, a licensing regulator, nor a venture capital fund, which makes the other options near-miss distractors.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: 'Most consequential change': Kevin Warsh says AI will reshape US economy, warns of a 'bumpy' road ahead
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional detail of a government scheme, in the style of UPSC's 'best describes the term' format questions on current schemes.

questions.stem: A District Collector in Chittoor called for collective efforts to eradicate child marriages. In this context, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The legal minimum age of marriage for women in India under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 is 18 years.
Statement-II: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, all child marriages are automatically void, regardless of whether either party exercises the option to annul it.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: the legal age of marriage for women is 18 years under the Act. Statement-II is incorrect because the Act makes child marriages voidable at the option of the child party (Section 3), not automatically void; only marriages procured through force, deceit, trafficking or enticement are declared void under Section 12.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: Chittoor Collector calls for collective efforts to eradicate child marriages
questions.pyqLink: Tests the voidable-versus-void distinction under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, a recurring nuance in UPSC's social legislation questions.

questions.stem: With reference to the revision of electoral rolls in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Article 324 of the Constitution vests the Election Commission with the power of superintendence, direction and control of elections, including the preparation of electoral rolls.
The Special Summary Revision (SSR) is a one-time exercise conducted only in years when general elections are due, whereas the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is carried out every year.
Under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, electoral rolls must be revised before every general election to the House of the People or a State Legislative Assembly.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Article 324 gives the EC overall authority over elections including rolls, and Section 21(2) of the RPA, 1950 mandates revision before every general election. Statement 2 reverses the facts — the SSR is the routine exercise normally conducted annually with January 1 as the qualifying date, while the SIR is the special, more intensive one-time exercise; the EC in fact skipped the SSR in 2026.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Special Summary Revision: What EC announcement means, how SSR differs from SIR
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 324 and the statutory basis of electoral roll revision under the RPA, 1950 — similar to UPSC questions on powers and functions of the Election Commission.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's crude oil imports:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: India imports more than 80% of its crude oil requirement, making it one of the world's largest crude oil importers.
India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves are maintained at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur.
Russia's share in India's crude oil import basket has risen continuously every month through 2026 without any decline.
The Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India imports over 80% of its crude requirement, and its Strategic Petroleum Reserves (under ISPRL) are located at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur. Statement 3 is wrong — Russia's share actually fell to about 44% in August 2026 from a high of 51% in July, so it has not risen continuously. Statement 4 is wrong because the PPAC functions under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, not the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India sourced more than two-thirds of its August oil imports from just three countries
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional knowledge of PPAC and India's strategic petroleum reserve system — comparable to UPSC questions on oil import dependency and energy security.

questions.stem: With reference to global biodiversity conservation efforts, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, adopted in 2022, includes a target to conserve at least 30% of the world's terrestrial and marine areas by 2030.
India has not endorsed the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework despite being a party to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the '30x30' target is a centrepiece of the Framework adopted at CBD COP15 in 2022. Statement 2 is incorrect: India, as a Party to the CBD, has endorsed the Framework and aligned its National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan with it, even as the UN flags that most countries remain off-track on these very targets.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: UN chief says 'subsidising fossil fuels is subsidising suicide'
questions.pyqLink: Tests the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and India's obligations under the CBD — similar to UPSC questions on COP15 biodiversity targets.

questions.stem: With reference to the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), which one of the following best describes its role?
options: It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Home Affairs responsible for licensing cybersecurity auditors.

It is the national nodal agency under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology mandated to collect, analyse and disseminate information on cyber incidents under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
It is an autonomous regulatory authority that certifies artificial intelligence systems before their commercial deployment in India.
It functions as the appellate tribunal for disputes arising under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
questions.explanation: CERT-In, established under Section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000, is the national nodal agency functioning under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology for cyber incident response, analysis and advisories — it was CERT-In that flagged the rogue AI agent breaches. It is not a licensing body under the Home Ministry, not an AI-certification authority, and not an appellate tribunal (that role lies elsewhere under the IT Act).
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: How rogue AI agents targeted Indian firms and accessed sensitive data
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory basis and nodal ministry of CERT-In under the IT Act, 2000 — relevant to UPSC's recurring focus on cyber-security institutions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements in the context of India-China trade:
statements: Statement-I: India has consistently sought greater market access in China for exports such as generic pharmaceuticals, bovine meat and other agricultural products, but progress has remained limited.
Statement-II: Under the WTO's Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) Agreement, member countries are barred from imposing any health-related import restrictions on agricultural goods.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct — India has long sought market access in China for generics, bovine meat and perishables, with limited success, as reiterated by the Finance Minister. Statement-II is incorrect because the SPS Agreement does not bar sanitary/phytosanitary measures outright; it permits them provided they are science-based, necessary and not disguised trade restrictions — the very misuse India alleges China is making of such measures as a non-tariff barrier.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Non-tariff barriers are biggest hurdle in India-China trade, says Nirmala Sitharaman
questions.pyqLink: Tests the WTO's SPS Agreement framework underlying 'non-tariff barriers' — similar to UPSC questions on WTO agreements (SPS, TBT, TRIPS).

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding caste-based reservation in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Article 16(4) guarantees a fundamental right to reservation that is enforceable by courts through a writ of mandamus.
The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 restricts Scheduled Caste status to persons professing the Hindu, Sikh or Buddhist religion.
The Supreme Court has held that backwardness associated with a person's pre-conversion caste status can be carried forward to claim reservation benefits in the religion to which the person converts.
The Mandal Commission recommended reservation for Other Backward Classes based on social and educational backwardness.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 confines SC status to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists, and the Mandal Commission based OBC reservation on social and educational backwardness. Statement 1 is wrong — the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney held Article 16(4) is an enabling provision, not a fundamental right enforceable by mandamus. Statement 3 is wrong because the Supreme Court recently held the opposite — backwardness from a pre-conversion status cannot be carried forward into the religion converted to.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: How religious conversion affects eligibility for caste-based reservation
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 16(4), the Scheduled Castes Order 1950 and the Indra Sawhney ruling — similar to UPSC questions on reservation jurisprudence.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
questions.explanation: The first three pairs are correctly matched: PPAC functions under the Petroleum Ministry, DIPAM (which handled the IDBI Bank stake sale) sits under the Finance Ministry, and BS emission norms are notified by the Road Transport Ministry. The fourth pair is wrong — the PMI is a private-sector survey compiled by S&P Global, not the RBI, and serves as a forward-looking indicator of business activity.

questions.sourceTitle: IDBI Bank sale: What deal means for India’s larger disinvestment plans

questions.stem: The Allahabad High Court has directed Uttar Pradesh to complete panchayat elections within three months under the existing reservation framework. In this context, consider the following statements about Panchayati Raj Institutions:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 inserted Part IX into the Constitution, giving Panchayats constitutional status.
Article 243D constitutionally mandates reservation of seats for Other Backward Classes in every Panchayat, in the same manner as for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Under Article 243K, it is the State Election Commission, and not the Election Commission of India, that is vested with superintendence, direction and control of elections to Panchayats.
The Constitution requires that elections to constitute a new Panchayat be completed before the expiry of the five-year term of the outgoing Panchayat.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct constitutional facts. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 243D(6) only enables states to provide OBC reservation at their discretion; unlike SC/ST reservation it is not constitutionally mandatory, which is exactly why UP needed a separate commission to decide its OBC quota.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: UP panchayat polls in 3 months: What happens to OBC quota, and what next
questions.pyqLink: Tests Part IX provisions (Articles 243D, 243E, 243K) on Panchayati Raj; similar to UPSC 2015 question on Panchayati Raj institutions' constitutional status.

questions.stem: With reference to the revision of electoral rolls by the Election Commission of India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Under Special Intensive Revision (SIR), existing electors must submit fresh enumeration forms, whereas under Special Summary Revision (SSR), their names automatically carry over to the new rolls without additional documents.

The power exercised by the Election Commission of India to revise electoral rolls under Article 324 extends to elections for Panchayats and Municipalities as well, since the Constitution does not create a separate authority for local body elections.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct and matches the described difference between SIR and SSR. Statement 2 is wrong: Articles 243K and 243ZA create separate State Election Commissions for Panchayats and Municipalities, so the ECI's Article 324 power does not cover local body polls.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Why Congress is highlighting 'machine-readable voter list', with ECI's new directive

questions.stem: With reference to the political career of Lal Krishna Advani, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: He served as Deputy Prime Minister of India in the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led NDA government.
He launched the Ram Rath Yatra in 1990 from Ayodhya, which was halted following his arrest in Bihar.
He was conferred the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2024.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Ram Rath Yatra began from Somnath, not Ayodhya (Ayodhya was its destination), before being halted by his arrest in Samastipur, Bihar.

pairs: Grouping including Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, since expanded to include other invited members
Trilateral forum of India, Brazil and South Africa for South-South cooperation
Grouping of India, Israel, the UAE and the United States for economic cooperation
Regional grouping whose Foreign Ministers' meeting was hosted by India in Kerala

questions.sourceTitle: Sudhakar Dalela, architect of BRICS consensus, appointed next envoy to Nepal

questions.stem: With reference to technologies used in digitising physical records such as electoral rolls, which one of the following best describes 'Optical Character Recognition (OCR)'?
options: A cryptographic technique that encrypts scanned documents to prevent unauthorised tampering with digital records
A technology that enables machines to detect and convert printed or handwritten text within images into machine-encoded, editable and searchable text
A biometric authentication method that verifies an individual's identity using unique facial or fingerprint patterns
A database indexing method that compresses large files to reduce storage space without altering their content
questions.explanation: OCR is pattern-recognition technology that converts scanned/printed text into machine-readable, searchable digital text, which is why it is being used to make voter lists machine-readable. It is not encryption, biometrics, or a compression technique, which rules out the other options.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Why Congress is highlighting 'machine-readable voter list', with ECI's new directive
questions.pyqLink: Tests a basic digital/IT technology concept similar to UPSC 2019's question on 'Merchant Discount Rate' style term-identification questions.

questions.stem: With reference to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) registered by the ED is legally equivalent to a First Information Report (FIR) and must mandatorily be supplied to the accused before arrest.
The ED is empowered under the PMLA to investigate the offence of money laundering, defined as any process or activity connected with proceeds of crime, including projecting it as untainted property.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 correctly reflects the Section 3 PMLA definition of money laundering and the ED's investigative mandate. Statement 1 is wrong: the Supreme Court (Vijay Madanlal Choudhary, 2022) held that an ECIR is an internal document of the ED and is not the legal equivalent of a police FIR, so it need not be supplied to the accused in the same manner.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: ED summons Pinarayi Vijayan after Supreme Court turns down urgent hearing on FIR challenge
questions.pyqLink: Tests the legal architecture of anti-money laundering enforcement (PMLA/ED), relevant to Economy syllabus on financial regulation; builds on the ECIR-vs-FIR distinction clarified by the Supreme Court.
